label: prose:intro-atom-isotope-knots
html: Every neutral atom or isotope (Z, N) is represented by a canonical closed braid in H_{3(Z+N)}(q) formed by embedding Z proton and N neutron Borromean blocks along the inter-nucleon connector permutation w_{\mathrm{inter}}. This section proves the existence and uniqueness of the normal-form representative T_w via the Diamond Lemma for the Hecke algebra, establishes decidability of the integer-linear-programming stability predicate, and defines the unstable atoms for which it fails.
